case_name: Oma @ Omprakash & Anr v State Of Tamil Nadu

State Of Tamil Nadu
Supreme Court of India

CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 143 OF 2007
The Judgment was delivered by : K. S. Radhakrishnan, J.
1. Appellants, herein, were awarded death sentence by the trial court after having found them guilty under Sections 395, 396 and 397 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'). They were sentenced to death by hanging under sub-s. 5 of S. 354 of Criminal Procedure Code for offences committed u/s. 396 IPC. facts: Appellants, herein, were awarded death sentence by the trial court after having found them guilty under Sections 395, 396 and 397 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').

The appellants and nine other absconding accused persons entered the house of one Lakshmi (PW 2) at 1 O' clock in the night of 07.06.1995 with the intention of committing burglary with iron rods in their hands and burgled 17 tolas of gold and Rs.5,000/- in cash.
It was alleged that they had strangulated Doctor Mohan Kumar, husband of PW 2 with a rope and thereby killed him.
A2 was arrested on 26.02.2005 in connection with some other case in Cr. No. 59 of 1996.
A1 was arrested on 21.09.2005 by the special team in connection with some other case in Cr. No. 352 of 2004 of Sri Perumbatoor Police Station.
The prosecution examined 15 witnesses to prove the case against the accused persons.
The trial court, as already indicated, convicted both the accused persons on 21.04.2006 for the offences under Sections 395, 396 and 397 IPC.
issues: Whether the trial court and High Court committed a grave error in convicting the accused persons?
Whether the prosecution miserably failed to prove the case against the appellant beyond reasonable doubt?
petitioner_arguments: The trial court and the High Court had committed a grave error in convicting the accused persons.
The prosecution miserably failed to prove the case against the appellant beyond reasonable doubt.
respondent_arguments: There is no fixed rule with regard to the period within which test identification parade be held.
Even in the absence of test identification parade, the identification of accused persons by the witnesses in court is a substantive piece of evidence.
court_reasoning: The tests laid down by this Court for determining the rarest of rare cases were completely overlooked by the Sessions Court.

The Sessions Judge had gone astray in referring to the views expressed by the then Chief Justice of Madras in a lecture delivered at Madurai, which advice according to the Sessions Judge was taken note of by another learned Judge in delivering a judgment in rowdy panchayat system.
holding: The Court is unhappy with the manner in which the Sessions Court awarded death sentence in the instant case.
The Court sets aside the conviction and sentence imposed by the trial court and the High Court and acquits the accused persons.
